failure_modes.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
failure_modes.evidence: In hop 1, the solver extensively analyzes passages [3-7] which concern Lee Jun-ho (footballer), Michelle Lee (singer), Bohemian (band), Park Kwang-su (filmmaker), and Son Jun-ho (actor). These passages are clearly irrelevant to the claim about Jay Park, 2PM, and Lee Jun-ho (singer). The reasoning section explicitly lists 'Passages [3-7]: Contain information about other individuals but are not directly relevant to the claim.' Despite recognizing irrelevance, the solver lists all passages in detail rather than focusing verification effort.

failure_modes.name: Query_Form_Mismatch
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 2 query: 'What 2PM music videos and songs were released after 2010? Does 2PM have a video or song called "Take Off"? When was the 2PM "Take Off" video released? What is 2PM's complete discography and filmography including all official music videos and their release dates?' This is a compound multi-part query bundling four separate questions (yes/no questions, when-questions, and what-questions) rather than a focused entity-targeted retrieval query.

failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 3 query '2PM Take Off single release date' seeks the exact same information already retrieved in hop 2. The 'Take Off (2PM song)' document with release date May 18, 2011 appears in hop 2 retrieval results (passage [2]) and reappears in hop 3 results. Summary_2 already states 'The claim is fully verified' with the Take Off release date, yet hop 3 re-asks for this same date.
